subject: Retention footprint: what persists after an interactive session (Fortis procurement follow-up)

Cc: procurement@fortis.com

Subject: Clarification needed — what Redwood stores by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — procurement is picking up the security questionnaire and we hit a few questions we need to confirm for our internal SRE/compliance gates. Can you please confirm, at a high level, Redwood's default retention behavior for the following items when using the hosted API (no special opt-ins):

- User requests / prompts (raw user input)
- Model responses (final completions)
- Partial/streamed token fragments during an interactive session
- Function/tool call payloads and structured JSON outputs (are these treated as responses?)
- KV cache or transient session state (for streaming/long-running sessions)
- Attachments or files uploaded as part of a request (how are those handled by default?)

We are aiming for a short, actionable summary that we can paste into the questionnaire. If you can also attach the Fortis-specific QA spreadsheet you mentioned and confirm residency options (us/eu/apac) and whether you can provide deletion evidence, that would be very helpful.

Thanks — appreciate a concise reply we can share with our procurement/legal teams.

Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise default summary suitable for procurement. I copied Marissa (solutions) and Kimberly (legal/compliance) for visibility — we'll attach the completed Fortis QA spreadsheet in the next message and include deletion proof options where required.

Default retention summary (hosted API, no customer opt-in):

- User requests / prompts: Not stored by default for hosted private sessions. Short-lived routing metadata is kept for 0–24 hours for debugging and then purged unless the customer enables "store-requests".
- Model responses / completions: Retained by default for 45 days to support troubleshooting, analytics, and quality monitoring. Customers can request shorter windows or opt-out at the account level.
- Streaming token fragments: Treated as ephemeral buffer material — fragments are not materialized as persisted records after the session ends. If a session is explicitly recorded (customer flag), fragments are assembled and persisted as part of the session transcript.
- Function/tool call payloads & structured outputs: Treated as model outputs. By default these are included in the 45-day retention window, because they are often necessary to reproduce behavior. Customers can configure selective redaction for PII within structured outputs.
- KV cache / session state: Ephemeral; KV caches are flushed automatically within 48 hours of last activity and are not included in the default persistent logs.
- Attachments/files sent with a request: By default attachments are proxied through the platform and stored only if the customer uses the Redwood-managed artifact store. If a customer opts to host attachments in their own S3/GCS, Redwood stores only a transient reference. We recommend customers use a managed bucket for sensitive files and enable lifecycle policies there.

Residency & deletion evidence:

- Residency: Hosted regions available: us, eu, apac. Fortis can be provisioned into a US region (us-east-1) for default hosted procurement pilots.
- Deletion evidence: We can provide deletion receipts (time-stamped job id + manifest) for records removed via our erasure runbook. For Reserved/Private deployments we can produce logs for audit review and an export showing erased object ids.

Next steps: Marissa will attach the Fortis-specific QA spreadsheet and the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for signature. Kimberly, can you confirm whether the deletion receipts wording below is sufficient for Fortis's procurement?

K

Karthik — quick follow-ups (procurement asks for explicit phrasing):

1) When you say "model responses retained 45 days": does that include sub-objects like tool / function outputs, and any JSON metadata produced by the model? We need a single sentence we can copy into our security questionnaire.
2) For streamed tokens, will Fortis ever see partial fragments in logs (e.g., session replay) if we do not enable session recording? We need to be clear that streaming by itself doesn't create a long-lived artifact.

(Quoting your note for context)
> - Function/tool call payloads & structured outputs: Treated as model outputs. By default these are included in the 45-day retention window, because they are often necessary to reproduce behavior. Customers can configure selective redaction for PII within structured outputs.

Please reply with two short sentences we can paste into the questionnaire.

Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks, and good clarifying questions. Below are two single-sentence answers your procurement team can paste into the questionnaire. I've attached the Fortis_Security_QA.xlsx with the same language and included the Mutual Action Plan for signature.

1) "By default, structured tool/function outputs and accompanying JSON metadata are treated as model outputs and are retained for a 45-day troubleshooting and analytics window unless Fortis configures a shorter retention or applies selective redaction."

2) "Streaming alone does not create a long-lived artifact — partial token fragments are ephemeral and are not persisted after the session ends unless Fortis explicitly enables session recording, in which case a session transcript is materialized and retained per the configured retention window."

Next actions: please confirm preferred US region (we recommend us-east-1 for latency) and return the signed MAP; once signed we will provision a trial environment scoped to Fortis and provide a deletion-receipt example.
